answer_sentences.text: RBI’s direction is that a UCB should not add penal interest to the loan’s interest rate; instead, any penalty for non-compliance must be treated as penal charges, not capitalised, and interest on unpaid amounts stays at the contracted rate until remediation.
answer_sentences.quote: "Penalty, if charged, for non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan contract by the borrower shall be treated as ‘penal charges’ and shall not be levied in the form of ‘penal interest’ that is added to the rate of interest charged on the advances. There shall be no capitalisation of penal charges, i.e., no further interest computed on such charges."

answer_sentences.text: If a UCB does impose penal charges, it cannot levy additional fresh penal charges on the earlier outstanding amount of those penal charges.
answer_sentences.quote: "Additional / fresh penal charges shall not be levied on the earlier outstanding amount of penal charges."
